title: Cyberattack disrupts blood storage refrigeration systems in France
content_md: France's national blood service has confirmed that a cyberattack targeting a refrigeration equipment provider raised temperature and defrost settings at three of its facilities, threatening stored blood products. The French Blood Establishment (Établissement français du sang or EFS), which manages blood collection, processing, and distribution across France, said the incident occurred on November 2 and affected systems used to monitor and control cold-storage chambers. According to a statement published on November 3, EFS was not directly targeted in the cyberattack, but was instead its refrigeration supplier. While EFS has not named the affected supplier, European refrigeration equipment provider Coolworld Rentals confirmed in a statement that a cybersecurity incident involving remote monitoring software had affected a limited number of its refrigeration units. Coolworld says the attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party component, which was outside the company's direct control. "The vulnerability currently being reported in the media relates to a component from a third-party supplier and was outside Coolworld's direct control," the company said. "Only a limited number of Coolworld units were affected, and Coolworld responded promptly and took appropriate measures." The company said it is working with affected customers but will not comment on individual cases.
